units.translation: I conjectured that the same reading should be restored, about which I spoke in the Preface to the fifth Leipzig edition p. LXIII. In the copies (for in M this part of the play is lost) is read πάρεστι σιγᾶς ἄτιμος. ἀλοίδορος ἥδιστος ἀφεμένων ἰδεῖν [it is possible to see the silence dishonored, unreviled, sweetest of those released]. Karsten had conjectured πάρεστι σιγὰς ἀτίμους ἀλοιδόρους αἴστους ἐφημένων ἰδεῖν [it is possible to see the silences dishonored, unreviled, unseen of those who sit upon].
unless this verse was inserted into the Agamemnon from the Persians, which Salzmann conjectured.
where άϊστον [unseen] indicates the effect of the verb αποτρέψειεν [may turn away].
it is possible to see the silence dishonored, unreviled, unseen of those who sit upon,
who will cast him out unseen from tyranny and thrones.
and when one is among the unseen, there is no defense.

let us not bring shame upon ourselves, but pleasure to my enemies.
shame for the Persians and shrill lamentations.
Schol. αἰσχρὰ ποιεῖν ἀναγκάζουσα [compelling to do shameful things].
shameful-planning, wretched, maddening, first cause of woe.
for it is shameful for a wise man to err.
for he is idle in shameful things, but loves not to be base.
and of evils and shameful things you will not speak of any glory.
more probable is οἰκτρῶς [pitifully], which I restored from the copies.
and shamefully in the veils of the councilors.
they died shamefully by a most inglorious fate,
he died shamefully, a cheat of money.

In M ὀδύρομαι [I lament], but with γρ. αἰσχύνομαι [I am ashamed] written in the margin, which some copies have in the text.

shaming the bed of her husband.

nor am I ashamed to hold this faithless anarchy in the city.
and yet even as I speak I am ashamed.
